title: A contract imposes a cyber requirement and nothing has been sent to the other party.
detail: The cyber module records that a contract requires cyber cover, and the contract module records that nothing has been sent as evidence. Those are two halves of the same problem held in different places: one module knows the obligation exists and the other knows it has not been discharged. Sending something is not the end of it either. A certificate cannot say anything that is not the same as what is stated in the insurance policy, and a certificate holder may not use the certificate holder box to imply or confer any new or additional rights beyond what the policy or an executed endorsement provides [S:tdi-certificates-of-insurance-faq]. So the evidence that satisfies a cyber requirement is the policy and any endorsement, not the certificate describing them.
action: Establish the evidence due date from the contract, then ask your broker for the cyber policy declarations and any endorsement the requirement calls for, rather than sending a certificate alone.
author: Aaron Bollinger
